Hi Ollie, it's Nina from the physio clinic. I'm just calling about your plan for the next two weeks. The good news is that the ankle is healing well. The swelling is going down. So, here are the rules. If it hurts, you stop. Every time. Pain is your body talking to you. For the first three days, you rest. If you walk a lot, the ankle gets swollen again, so keep it up on a chair when you sit. Ice it three times a day, for fifteen minutes, not more. From day four, you start the stretches on the sheet. If they feel easy, great. If your ankle feels sore the next morning, you did too much. And no surfing for two weeks. I know. Surfers always ask. The answer is still no. Call me if you have any questions.

Okay everyone, quick one before we paddle out. Ollie is recovering, and he's coming to training next week. He can't go in the water, but he's going to help me on the sand, so be nice to him. And after Saturday, we have a new rule. Everybody warms up before training. Every time, no excuses. Ten minutes on the sand: run, stretch your legs, stretch your shoulders. The physio says that if your muscles are cold, you get hurt more easily. It's true. If you jump in the water cold, your shoulders get sore after twenty minutes. And one more thing. If somebody gets hurt, the closest person stays with them, and one person gets an adult. That's the plan. Right, ten minutes. Go.
